body.statement:
Does the statistical model \(\mathfrak M\) establish both premises of \(\mathrm{prop{:}balanced\text{-}grid\text{-}argmin\text{-}transfer}\) with the candidate functions \(A\) and \(B\)?  Concretely, can one prove the compact-window limit
\[
\sup_{\substack{m\in\mathcal M_n\\ a\leq m/\sqrt n\leq b}}
\left|n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)
-\max_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\{A(\beta)m/\sqrt n+B(\beta)\sqrt n/m\}\right|
\longrightarrow0
\]
for every \(0<a<b<\infty\), together with sequential coercivity for bounded pilots, \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\), positive pilot fractions with \(N\asymp n\), and \(N=o(n)\)?  The nearly-all-pilot case \(N=o(n)\) is proved, but the remaining cases require the finite-boundary comparison and the pilot-information-to-action bridge.

obligation.what_is_open: The compact-window second-order risk approximation that links the statistical model to the deterministic envelope.
obligation.obstruction: The exact decomposition contains only deletion and action-loss components, but neither candidate frontier coefficient is proved uniformly at the required scale.
obligation.attempted: Proved the component identity, the first-order oracle gain, and the conditional balanced-grid argmin theorem; these isolate the remaining finite-boundary and information-to-action work.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact risk identity and the deterministic argmin transfer are proved.  The statistical compact-window premise reduces to showing, uniformly for \(m/\sqrt n\) in compact subsets of \((0,\infty)\),
\[
D_{n,m}(\beta)
=A(\beta)\frac m{n^2}
+o(n^{-3/2}),
\qquad
L_{n,m}(\widehat G_m,\beta)
=\frac{B(\beta)}{nm}
+o(n^{-3/2}),
\]
together with the matching arbitrary-action lower comparison.  Neither coefficient-level statement follows from the first-order oracle gain.

body.justification: This question is the honest headline status of sharp pilot sizing.
body.gap: Compact-window second-order convergence and four endpoint lower comparisons remain unresolved.
body.consumer: No preregistered square-root pilot recommendation is certified until this question is answered.
